name: agent-worktrees
description: Run and monitor multiple Claude Code agents across your git worktrees from a single side panel.

agentWorktrees.trace.description: Log every external call (each git command and GitHub API request, with its duration and result) to the "Agent Worktrees" output channel. Turn this on to diagnose slow or failing git/GitHub activity, then open View: Output and pick "Agent Worktrees". Off by default.

enumDescriptions: Needs you: a permission prompt or a question
Processing a prompt, or running a tool or shell command
Started, or finished responding and awaiting you

agentWorktrees.agentStatusOrder.markdownDescription: Which order the **agents view** groups its rows in. Waiting first by default, so the agent that needs you is at the top whatever worktree it is in. Edit it here or in Settings → Preferences in the panel. A partial or unrecognized list is completed with the missing statuses rather than hiding those agents.

enumDescriptions: Never. The pulsing dot, the collapsed-group badge and the Activity Bar count are the only signals.
Only while the VS Code window is not focused, which is when nothing else reaches you.
Every time an agent starts waiting, focused or not.
agentWorktrees.notifyWaiting.markdownDescription: Show a notification with an **Open terminal** button when an agent starts waiting for you. One notification per agent, so two agents prompting at the same time raise two, each opening its own terminal. Raised once per time an agent starts waiting, never repeated while it stays there, and never for agents that were already waiting when the window opened.

agentWorktrees.statusPollSeconds.markdownDescription: How often, in seconds, to re-run `git status` for a worktree that has an agent working in it *and* is not open in the Source Control view. Worktrees that are open there are not polled at all: they refresh on the Git extension's own change event. Lower is fresher, higher spawns less git, which matters most on Windows where every process spawn is expensive.
